Database Transactions

Transactions give applications a disciplined model for coordinating related database changes.

Isolation levels trade implementation cost for stronger guarantees about concurrent behavior.

Applications still need idempotency when requests may be retried by clients or infrastructure.

Careful schema design reduces contention on the most frequently updated records.

Production metrics should expose lock waits, abort rates, and unusually long transactions.
